subject: Observability add-ons: retention/tracing/advanced dashboards — pricing & rebate discussion
messages:
From: Alex Soto <alex.soto@novamed.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: NovaMed Procurement <procurement@novamed.com>
Date: 2028-09-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Observability add-ons pricing for renewal

Marissa,

Hope youre well. As we pull together our renewal for the platform (contract anniversary in November), procurement asked me to reach out early on add-on pricing for observability: specifically retention (longer horizons for logs/metrics), tracing (span ingest and storage), and the advanced dashboards pack.

High level ask: can Redwood propose a consolidated rebate or committed pricing arrangement that covers all three add-ons? NovaMed is considering a two-year commit for base inference + observability if we can reach a predictable unit price and concession for the first 12 months while we ramp. Our rough target is a rebate in the mid-teens (15% range) conditional on a 24-month committed spend.

I attached our Q3 usage export for the three products so you can see current baseline and ramp assumptions (usage_profile_q3.csv).

Can you share an outline of structures youd consider (tiered commit, onboarding credits, milestone rebates)? Also can you send a draft SOW so procurement can review timelines and onboarding credits?

Thanks,
Alex Soto
Procurement Program Manager
NovaMed

Attachments: usage_profile_q3.csv (csv)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Soto <alex.soto@novamed.com>, NovaMed Procurement <procurement@novamed.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-09-18T11:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Observability add-ons pricing for renewal

Alex —

Thanks for the data and the clear ask. Quick replies to the specific requests:

1) Structures we typically offer:
- Committed spend tiers with corresponding unit discounts on observability add-ons (retention, tracing, dashboards).
- Time-limited onboarding credits (one-time) to offset migration and dashboard build costs.
- Conditional milestone rebates that pay out quarterly as usage hits defined ramp thresholds.

2) Typical ranges: we can explore 10–18% effective rebate depending on term length, commit level, and whether onboarding credits are required.

3) Next steps: Ill loop in Ben for the discount schedule and Kim for billing/legal constraints. Im attaching a draft SOW for schedule and deliverables (redwood_draft_sow_v1.pdf). Please review the milestones section and call out any compliance or procurement constraints.

A couple quick clarifying questions that will shape the pricing model:
- For retention: what percentage of your logs/metrics need >90-day retention versus archival-only?
- For tracing: how many peak daily span writes should we size for (average + spike)?
- For dashboards: are these per-seat or org-wide visual dashboards (that affects seat-based vs. ingestion pricing)?

If it helps, we can schedule a 30-minute call tomorrow to walk through a provisional discount schedule.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
redwood.com

Attachments: redwood_draft_sow_v1.pdf (pdf)
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-09-19T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Observability add-ons pricing for renewal

Marissa — adding my recommended structure here so we have something concrete to share with NovaMed. I reviewed the usage export and sketched the following example schedules.

Proposed discount & rebate schedule (example):
- 12-month commit (baseline): 8% rebate on observability add-on line items; onboarding credit = $25k one-time to assist dashboard builds.
- 24-month commit: 12% rebate baseline; if actual consumption >= 100% of committed monthly average for 3 consecutive quarters, additional +4% rebate (total 16%).
- 36-month commit: 14% rebate baseline; additional +4% accelerated rebate gated by ramp milestones.

Milestone payout mechanics: quarterly true-up. If monthly consumption < 85% of committed baseline for two consecutive quarters, rebates are prorated/held until catch-up cadence.

Notes on product mappings:
- Retention: price per GB-month with bucketed tiers; deeper retention gives lower per-GB price.
- Tracing: price per million spans ingested with a separate storage multiplier for retained spans.
- Dashboards: combination of seats + advanced visualization fee; onboarding credit is primarily to offset dashboard build hours.

Ive attached the cleaned usage_profile_q3.csv with our annotations and a quick model. If NovaMed prefers a simpler flat rebate tied to committed spend rather than milestones, we can create a fallback option.

Ben
Account Lead — Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

Attachments: usage_profile_q3.csv (annotated)
From: Alex Soto <alex.soto@novamed.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: NovaMed Procurement <procurement@novamed.com>
Date: 2028-09-21T10:17:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Observability add-ons pricing for renewal

Marissa —

Thanks for the quick turn and Ben for the detailed schedule. Procurement reviewed and came back with a counter-proposal: NovaMed can agree to a 24-month commit, but wed prefer a simpler, flat rebate structure that is easier for our finance team to forecast. Proposed counter: 12% flat rebate on observability add-ons across the two years, plus a $20k onboarding credit. Wed also like a protective rollback clause: if usage drops below 70% of the committed baseline for two consecutive quarters, Redwood can proportionally step down the rebate for the remainder of the term rather than retroactively clawing back paid rebates.

Weve put a DocuSign link in our procurement system for a term sheet so we can move quickly if we reach alignment: https://app.docusign.com/envelope/ABCDEFG12345

On the carveouts: we will be ok with milestone-based accelerators but prefer them to be additive (bonus rebate) rather than the only mechanism for reaching the 12% target.

Can Redwood produce a revised term sheet that reflects the 12% flat rebate + $20k credit with the rollback guard language? If so we can get it to legal next week.

Alex
Procurement Program Manager, NovaMed

Subject: Re: Observability add-ons pricing for renewal — MAP and next steps

Alex —

Appreciate the clarity and the counter. Summary / agreed pivot for a revised term sheet well draft today:

- Term: 24 months.
- Observability add-ons: flat 12% rebate across retention, tracing, advanced dashboards.
- Onboarding credit: $20,000 one-time to support dashboard and trace onboarding.
- Rollback protection: if usage falls below 70% of committed baseline for two consecutive quarters, Redwood will proportionally step down rebates for future invoices rather than claw back rebates already paid.
- Optional accelerator: additive milestone rebate up to +3% if monthly consumption >= 110% of committed baseline for two consecutive quarters (quarterly true-up).

Action items / MAP:
1) Redwood (Marissa + Ben): issue revised term sheet and updated SOW reflecting the $20k credit and rollback language. I will attach the updated redwood_draft_sow_v1.pdf and term sheet to the HubSpot deal and send for your procurement review by EOD.
2) NovaMed: review with legal and confirm if DocuSign envelope is acceptable; if so confirm signer details.
3) Schedule: target sign by Oct 6 to hit onboarding window before November anniversary.

Proposed call: Tuesday 9/26 10:00am PT to finalize term sheet. If that works, Ill send calendar invite.

Thanks all — well move quickly once NovaMed confirms legal preferences.

Best,
Marissa Cole
